note.explanation: Rest and motion describe whether an object's position changes compared with its surroundings. The same object can be at rest compared with one observer and in motion compared with another.
examples: A parked motorcycle is at rest compared with a nearby tree.
A passenger sitting in a moving train is at rest compared with other passengers, but in motion compared with someone standing on the platform.
note.checkAnswer: The passenger is at rest with respect to the other passengers, but in motion with respect to the observer on the platform.
note.simple: Ask: “Is the object's position changing compared with this observer and these surroundings?” The answer may change when the observer changes.
note.checkQuestion: A passenger is sitting in a moving train. Is the passenger at rest or in motion compared with someone standing on the platform?
note.title: Rest and motion depend on the observer
steps: Choose the object and the observer.
Compare the object's position with its surroundings.
If its position does not change, it is at rest with respect to those surroundings.
If its position continuously changes, it is in motion with respect to those surroundings.
note.answer: Rest or motion is decided by comparing an object's position with its surroundings.

options: It is at rest with respect to the tree.
It is in motion with respect to the tree.
It is at rest with respect to every observer.
Its state cannot be described.
mcqs.stem: A car is parked beside a tree. How is the car described with respect to the tree?
rationales: This is correct because the car's position does not change compared with the tree.
This is incorrect because the car's position is not changing compared with the tree.
This is incorrect because rest and motion depend on the surroundings and observer.
This is incorrect because the car's state can be described relative to the tree.

options: At rest with respect to the platform observer
In motion with respect to the platform observer
At rest with respect to every observer
Neither at rest nor in motion
mcqs.stem: A passenger sits in a moving train. What is the passenger's state with respect to an observer standing on the platform?
rationales: This is incorrect because the passenger's position changes compared with the platform observer.
This is correct because the train carries the passenger past the platform observer.
This is incorrect because the passenger is not at rest with respect to all observers.
This is incorrect because the passenger is in motion with respect to the platform observer.

options: A body is at rest if its position does not change with respect to its surroundings.
A body is at rest if it has no mass.
A body is in motion if it changes its shape.
A body is in motion only if its speed increases.
mcqs.stem: Which statement correctly describes a body at rest?
rationales: This is correct and follows the definition of rest in this section.
This is incorrect because mass does not decide whether a body is at rest.
This is incorrect because a change of shape alone does not define motion here.
This is incorrect because a body can move at constant speed.

options: The motorcycle's position is changing with respect to nearby surroundings.
The motorcycle has a large mass.
The motorcycle's engine is switched on.
The rider is looking ahead.
mcqs.stem: An observer says a motorcycle is in motion. Which observation supports this statement?
rationales: This is correct because motion means continuously changing position with respect to surroundings.
This is incorrect because mass does not show whether position is changing.
This is incorrect because an engine can be on while the motorcycle remains stationary.
This is incorrect because the rider's gaze does not determine the motorcycle's motion.

options: The passenger is at rest relative to the train and in motion relative to the road.
The passenger is in motion relative to the train and at rest relative to the road.
The passenger is at rest relative to both the train and the road.
The passenger is in motion relative to both the train and the road.
mcqs.stem: A passenger sits inside a moving train. Which description is correct?
rationales: This is correct because the passenger stays in the same position in the train but moves with it relative to the road.
This is incorrect because the passenger is not changing position relative to the train.
This is incorrect because the passenger's position changes relative to the road.
This is incorrect because the passenger is at rest relative to the train.

options: Whether an object is at rest or in motion depends on the reference surroundings.
Every object is always at rest.
Every object is always in motion.
Rest and motion depend only on an object's size.
mcqs.stem: What does it mean to say that rest and motion are relative?
rationales: This is correct because an object's state can differ for different observers and surroundings.
This is incorrect because objects can change position with respect to their surroundings.
This is incorrect because an object can be at rest relative to some surroundings.
This is incorrect because size does not determine rest or motion.

written.finalAnswer: A body is at rest if it does not change its position with respect to its surroundings. A body is in motion if it continuously changes its position with respect to its surroundings. Rest and motion are relative.

examTips: This topic is suitable for a definition or a short comparison question, such as differentiating between rest and motion.
For full marks, use the textbook phrases “with respect to its surroundings” and “continuously changes its position.”
A train-passenger example can explain why rest and motion are relative: state the observer for each description.

hints: First identify the point or surroundings used for comparison.
If the body's position stays unchanged compared with that point, it is at rest.
yourTurn.question: Q2.2. If a body does not change its position with respect to some fixed point, then it will be in a state of:  (a) rest (b) motion  (c) uniform motion (d) variable motion
solution: The body's position does not change with respect to a fixed point.
By the definition, it is at rest with respect to that point.
Therefore, the correct choice is (a) rest.

explain.title: Rest
explain.body: “If a body does not change its position with respect to its surroundings, it is said to be at rest.” Always name the surroundings or observer being used for the comparison.

explain.title: Motion
explain.body: “If a body continuously changes its position with respect to its surroundings, it is said to be in motion.” A moving motorcyclist changes position compared with nearby buildings, trees or poles.

explain.title: Rest and motion are relative
explain.body: “The state of rest or motion of a body is always relative.” A passenger seated in a moving train is at rest compared with other passengers, but in motion compared with a person standing on the platform.

mistakes: Writing that an object is simply at rest without saying with respect to what surroundings or observer.
Assuming an object must be at rest for every observer if it is at rest for one observer.
Confusing a body's own movement with its movement relative to a chosen point.
Leaving out the idea that position changes continuously when defining motion.
